selectedIdea.description: How WAL changes who has to wait
selectedIdea.rationale: How WAL changes who has to wait
selectedIdea.evidence: readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed concurrently.

narrative:
### Selected Story
Explain WAL through its effect on the relationship between reading and writing: readers do not block writers, and writers do not block readers. The reader should understand that these activities can proceed concurrently, rather than one having to wait for the other.

### Story Progression
- **Context:** Introduce WAL in relation to reading and writing happening at the same time.
- **Development:** Explain that readers do not block writers, and writers do not block readers.
- **Endpoint:** Clarify the central point: reading and writing can proceed concurrently.

### Critical Constraints
- Do not claim that WAL eliminates all waiting or describe how it achieves this; the supplied material establishes only that readers and writers do not block one another.

source: In 1989, NASA's Voyager 2 became the first-and only-spacecraft to study Neptune up close.

selectedIdea.title: An encounter no other spacecraft has repeated
selectedIdea.description: An encounter no other spacecraft has repeated
selectedIdea.rationale: An encounter no other spacecraft has repeated
selectedIdea.evidence: In 1989, NASA's Voyager 2 became the first-and only-spacecraft to study Neptune up close.

narrative:
### Selected Story
The story is about the singularity of Voyager 2’s close-up study of Neptune: in 1989, it became the first—and, according to the supplied material, the only—spacecraft to study the planet up close. The reader should understand that this encounter has not been repeated by another spacecraft.

### Story Progression
- **Context:** Establish Neptune as the subject and focus on spacecraft study of the planet up close.
- **Development:** Identify Voyager 2 and 1989 as the spacecraft and year of the close-up study.
- **Endpoint:** Clarify the central point: no other spacecraft has repeated that close-up study.

### Critical Constraints
- Do not speculate about why no other spacecraft has repeated the study or add claims about its effects or significance beyond its singularity.

narrative:
### Selected Story
The story is about a provision that connected a claim to land with the possibility of receiving its title: title was received before the five years of residence began. The reader should understand this as a conditional path from claim to ownership, not evidence that a particular claimant completed it.

### Story Progression
- **Context:** Introduce the land claim and the prospect of receiving title, without adding historical or legal background not supplied here.
- **Development:** Explain the stated condition: title was received before the five years of residence began.
- **Endpoint:** Clarify that the provision made continuous residence a requirement beginning after title.

### Critical Constraints
- Do not claim that a particular claimant fulfilled the residence requirement or received title.
